questions.q: Without using Parse JSON, how must you reference a field inside an HTTP action's JSON response body?
options: It's impossible to reference without a premium connector
It's automatically available as a token with no extra work
By writing a raw expression by hand in every action that needs it, with no autocomplete
By converting the flow to run in Azure Functions instead
questions.explain: Without a schema, Power Automate can't offer typed tokens for a JSON body's fields, so referencing one means hand-writing an expression like body('HTTP')?['field'] everywhere it's needed.

questions.q: What is the fast, recommended way to get a schema for Parse JSON?
options: Copy a schema from an unrelated flow and hope it matches
Use Generate from sample, pasting in a real example of the response payload
Schemas are not required by Parse JSON
Write the JSON Schema specification entirely by hand every time
questions.explain: Generate from sample builds a schema automatically from a real example payload you paste in, which is far faster and less error-prone than hand-writing JSON Schema.

questions.q: What problem does the Compose action solve?
options: It converts a flow into a scheduled trigger
It sends HTTP requests to external APIs
It replaces the need for a trigger entirely
It saves any input as a single, named, reusable output instead of retyping the same expression in multiple actions
questions.explain: Compose takes any input (a literal, expression, or earlier output) and produces one named output that later actions can reference by name, avoiding repeated expressions.

questions.q: How many fields do you configure on a Compose action?
options: Compose cannot be configured; it runs automatically
Three: Name, Type, Value
Five: Method, URI, Headers, Queries, Body
One: Inputs
questions.explain: Compose has a single field, Inputs, which accepts whatever value you want saved as its reusable output.

questions.q: In the classification example, what does running Parse JSON on the model's response body enable?
options: The response can only be viewed in run history, never used in actions
The category, confidence, and suggested_owner properties become usable tokens the flow can branch on or assign directly
The flow must restart from the trigger
The response is deleted after use
questions.explain: Once Parse JSON runs with a matching schema, each property in the payload becomes a typed token — confidence can feed a Condition, and suggested_owner can be used directly in a later action.
